- parallel(thunks: Array<() => Promise<any>>): Promise<any[]> — run tasks concurrently. This is a BARRIER: awaits all thunks before returning. A thunk that throws (or whose agent errors) resolves to `null` in the result array — the call itself never rejects, so `.filter(Boolean)` before using the results. Use ONLY when you genuinely need all results together.
- log(message: string): void — emit a progress message to the user (shown as a narrator line above the progress tree)
- phase(title: string): void — start a new phase; subsequent agent() calls are grouped under this title in the progress display
- args: any — the value passed as Workflow's `args` input, verbatim (undefined if not provided). Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values in the tool call, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — `args: ["a.ts", "b.ts"]`, not `args: "[\"a.ts\", ...]"` (a stringified list reaches the script as one string, so `args.filter`/`args.map` throw). Use this to parameterize named workflows — e.g. pass a research question, target path, or config object directly instead of via a side-channel file.
- budget: {total: number|null, spent(): number, remaining(): number} — the turn's token target from the user's "+500k"-style directive. `budget.total` is null if no target was set. `budget.spent()` returns output tokens spent this turn across the main loop and all workflows — the pool is shared, not per-workflow. `budget.remaining()` returns `max(0, total - spent())`, or `Infinity` if no target. The target is a HARD ceiling, not advisory: once `spent()` reaches `total`, further `agent()` calls throw. Use for dynamic loops: `while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) { ... }`, or static scaling: `const FLEET = budget.total ? Math.floor(budget.total / 100_000) : 5`.
- workflow(nameOrRef: string | {scriptPath: string}, args?: any): Promise<any> — run another workflow inline as a sub-step and return whatever it returns. Pass a name to invoke a saved workflow (same registry as {name: "..."}), or {scriptPath} to run a script file you Wrote earlier. The child shares this run's concurrency cap, agent counter, abort signal, and token budget — its agents appear under a "▸ name" group in /workflows and its tokens count toward budget.spent(). The args param becomes the child's `args` global. Nesting is one level only: workflow() inside a child throws. Throws on unknown name / unreadable scriptPath / child syntax error; catch to handle gracefully.

Subagents are told their final text IS the return value (not a human-facing message), so they return raw data. For structured output, use the schema option — validation happens at the tool-call layer so the model retries on mismatch.
Schemas need {type: 'object', properties: {...}} at root and required ⊆ properties; unsatisfiable ones throw at agent().

Workflow agents can reach all session-connected MCP tools via ToolSearch — schemas load on demand per agent. Caveat: interactively-authenticated MCP servers (e.g. claude.ai) may be absent in headless/cron runs.

Subagents get the same CLAUDE.md files injected at start that you did (except built-in agent types that omit them, such as Explore and Plan) — don't tell them to re-read those or paste their rules into the prompt; name the specific rule a stage needs, if any.

Scripts are plain JavaScript, NOT TypeScript — type annotations (`: string[]`), interfaces, and generics fail to parse. The script body runs in an async context — use await directly. Standard JS built-ins (JSON, Math, Array, etc.) are available — EXCEPT `Date.now()`/`Math.random()`/argless `new Date()`, which throw (they would break resume); pass timestamps in via `args`, stamp results after the workflow returns, and for randomness vary the agent prompt/label by index. No filesystem or Node.js API access.

DEFAULT TO pipeline(). Only reach for a barrier (parallel between stages) when you genuinely need ALL prior-stage results together.

A barrier is correct ONLY when stage N needs cross-item context from all of stage N-1:
- Dedup/merge across the full result set before expensive downstream work
- Early-exit if the total count is zero ("0 bugs found → skip verification entirely")
- Stage N's prompt references "the other findings" for comparison

A barrier is NOT justified by:
- "I need to flatten/map/filter first" — do it inside a pipeline stage: pipeline(items, stageA, r => transform([r]).flat(), stageB)
- "The stages are conceptually separate" — that's what pipeline() models. Separate stages ≠ synchronized stages.
- "It's cleaner code" — barrier latency is real. If 5 finders run and the slowest takes 3× the fastest, a barrier wastes 2/3 of the fast finders' idle time.

Smell test: if you wrote
  const a = await parallel(...)
  const b = transform(a)        // flatten, map, filter — no cross-item dependency
  const c = await parallel(b.map(...))
that middle transform doesn't need the barrier. Rewrite as a pipeline with the transform inside a stage. When in doubt: pipeline.

Concurrent agent() calls are capped at min(16, available CPUs - 2) per workflow — excess calls queue and run as slots free up. You can still pass 100 items to parallel()/pipeline() and they all complete; only ~10 run at any moment. Total agent count across a workflow's lifetime is capped at 1000 — a runaway-loop backstop set far above any real workflow. A single parallel()/pipeline() call accepts at most 4096 items; passing more is an explicit error, not a silent truncation.

When a barrier IS correct — dedup across all findings before expensive verification:
  const all = await parallel(DIMENSIONS.map(d => () => agent(d.prompt, {schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA})))
  const deduped = dedupeByFileAndLine(all.filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.findings))  // <-- genuinely needs ALL at once
  const verified = await parallel(deduped.map(f => () => agent(verifyPrompt(f), {schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})))

Loop-until-count pattern — accumulate to a target:
  const bugs = []
  while (bugs.length < 10) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length}/10 found`)
  }

Loop-until-budget pattern — scale depth to the user's "+500k" directive. Guard on budget.total: with no target set, remaining() is Infinity and the loop would run straight to the 1000-agent cap.
  const bugs = []
  while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length} found, ${Math.round(budget.remaining()/1000)}k remaining`)
  }

Composing patterns — exhaustive review (find → dedup vs seen → diverse-lens panel → loop-until-dry):
  const seen = new Set(), confirmed = []
  let dry = 0
  while (dry < 2) {                                              // loop-until-dry
    const found = (await parallel(FINDERS.map(f => () =>          // barrier: collect all finders this round
      agent(f.prompt, {phase: 'Find', schema: BUGS})))).filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.bugs)
    const fresh = found.filter(b => !seen.has(key(b)))           // dedup vs ALL seen — plain code, not an agent
    if (!fresh.length) { dry++; continue }
    dry = 0; fresh.forEach(b => seen.add(key(b)))
    const judged = await parallel(fresh.map(b => () =>           // every fresh bug judged concurrently...
      parallel(['correctness','security','repro'].map(lens => () =>   // ...each by 3 distinct lenses
        agent(`Judge "${b.desc}" via the ${lens} lens — real?`, {phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT})))
        .then(vs => ({ b, real: vs.filter(Boolean).filter(v => v.real).length >= 2 }))))
    confirmed.push(...judged.filter(v => v.real).map(v => v.b))
  }
  return confirmed
  // dedup vs `seen`, NOT `confirmed` — else judge-rejected findings reappear every round and it never converges.

Quality patterns — common shapes; pick by task and compose freely:
- Adversarial verify: spawn N independent skeptics per finding, each prompted to REFUTE. Kill if ≥majority refute. Prevents plausible-but-wrong findings from surviving.
    const votes = await parallel(Array.from({length: 3}, () => () =>
      agent(`Try to refute: ${claim}. Default to refuted=true if uncertain.`, {schema: VERDICT})))
    const survives = votes.filter(Boolean).filter(v => !v.refuted).length >= 2
- Perspective-diverse verify: when a finding can fail in more than one way, give each verifier a distinct lens (correctness, security, perf, does-it-reproduce) instead of N identical refuters — diversity catches failure modes redundancy can't.
- Judge panel: generate N independent attempts from different angles (e.g. MVP-first, risk-first, user-first), score with parallel judges, synthesize from the winner while grafting the best ideas from runners-up. Beats one-attempt-iterated when the solution space is wide.
- Loop-until-dry: for unknown-size discovery (bugs, issues, edge cases), keep spawning finders until K consecutive rounds return nothing new. Simple counters (while count < N) miss the tail.
- Multi-modal sweep: parallel agents each searching a different way (by-container, by-content, by-entity, by-time). Each is blind to what the others surface; useful when one search angle won't find everything.
- Completeness critic: a final agent that asks "what's missing — modality not run, claim unverified, source unread?" What it finds becomes the next round of work.
- No silent caps: if a workflow bounds coverage (top-N, no-retry, sampling), `log()` what was dropped — silent truncation reads as "covered everything" when it didn't.

Scale to what the user asked for. "find any bugs" → a few finders, single-vote verify. "thoroughly audit this" or "be comprehensive" → larger finder pool, 3–5 vote adversarial pass, synthesis stage. When unsure, lean toward thoroughness for research/review/audit requests and toward brevity for quick checks.

These patterns aren't exhaustive — compose novel harnesses when the task calls for it (tournament brackets, self-repair loops, staged escalation, whatever fits).

Use this tool for multi-step orchestration where control flow should be deterministic (loops, conditionals, fan-out) rather than model-driven.

## Resume

The tool result includes a runId. To resume after a pause, kill, or script edit, relaunch with Workflow({scriptPath, resumeFromRunId}) — the longest unchanged prefix of agent() calls returns cached results instantly; the first edited/new call and everything after it runs live. Same script + same args → 100% cache hit. Before diagnosing why a completed workflow returned an empty or unexpected result, Read <transcriptDir>/journal.jsonl — it records each agent's actual return value; do not assume cached results are non-empty. Date.now()/Math.random()/new Date() are unavailable in scripts (they would break this) — stamp results after the workflow returns, or pass timestamps via args. Fallback when no journal is available: Read agent-<id>.jsonl files in the transcript directory and hand-author a continuation script.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

1	"""Idempotent receipts binding a state to an audit record.
2	
3	A receipt only names an ``id`` and the two 64-char lowercase hex digests of
4	the state and audit record it binds; the state and audit bytes themselves
5	are never read or written here.  Receipts are kept in an index stored as
6	UTF-8 compact JSON::
7	
8	    {"items":[{"audit":...,"id":...,"state":...},...],"version":1}\\n
9	
10	The top-level keys are fixed in the order ``items`` then ``version`` and
11	``version`` is always the integer 1.  ``items`` is an array of records
12	sorted ascending by ``id`` (ids are unique); each record carries the str
13	keys ``id``, ``state`` and ``audit`` and is canonically encoded with the
14	key order ``audit``, ``id``, ``state``.  Non-ASCII characters are preserved
15	unescaped and the file ends with exactly one ``\\n``.
16	
17	A missing index file stands for an empty index; an existing file that
18	violates any byte, structure, order or field rule is corrupt.
19	"""
20	
21	from __future__ import annotations
22	
23	import json
24	import os
25	import re
26	from typing import Any
27	
28	AUDIT = "audit"
29	ID = "id"
30	STATE = "state"
31	
32	ITEMS = "items"
33	VERSION = "version"
34	
35	_RECEIPT_KEYS = (ID, STATE, AUDIT)
36	_RECORD_KEYS = (AUDIT, ID, STATE)
37	_INDEX_KEYS = (ITEMS, VERSION)
38	_INDEX_VERSION = 1
39	
40	_ID_RE = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}\Z")
41	_DIGEST_RE = re.compile(r"[0-9a-f]{64}\Z")
42	
43	
44	class CorruptReceiptError(ValueError):
45	    """The receipt index exists but its bytes are not a valid index."""
46	
47	
48	def _is_digest(value: Any) -> bool:
49	    return isinstance(value, str) and _DIGEST_RE.fullmatch(value) is not None
50	
51	
52	def _validated_receipt(receipt: Any) -> dict[str, str]:
53	    """Validate one receipt and return a fresh dict in record key order."""
54	    if not isinstance(receipt, dict):
55	        raise TypeError("receipt must be a dict")
56	    if set(receipt.keys()) != set(_RECEIPT_KEYS):
57	        raise ValueError(
58	            "receipt must contain exactly the keys 'id', 'state' and 'audit'"
59	        )
60	    for key in _RECEIPT_KEYS:
61	        if not isinstance(receipt[key], str):
62	            raise TypeError(f"receipt {key} must be a str")
63	    receipt_id = receipt[ID]
64	    if _ID_RE.fullmatch(receipt_id) is None:
65	        raise ValueError("receipt id must match [A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}")
66	    if not _is_digest(receipt[STATE]):
67	        raise ValueError("receipt state must be 64 lowercase hex characters")
68	    if not _is_digest(receipt[AUDIT]):
69	        raise ValueError("receipt audit must be 64 lowercase hex characters")
70	    return {AUDIT: receipt[AUDIT], ID: receipt_id, STATE: receipt[STATE]}
71	
72	
73	def _serialize_index(records: list[dict[str, str]]) -> bytes:
74	    ordered = [
75	        {AUDIT: record[AUDIT], ID: record[ID], STATE: record[STATE]}
76	        for record in records
77	    ]
78	    index = {ITEMS: ordered, VERSION: _INDEX_VERSION}
79	    text = json.dumps(index, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":")) + "\n"
80	    return text.encode("utf-8")
81	
82	
83	def _parse_index(raw: bytes) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
84	    """Validate every byte of a receipt index and return its records.
85	
86	    Raises :class:`CorruptReceiptError` for any UTF-8/JSON failure,
87	    non-canonical byte encoding, wrong key set or order, bad version,
88	    duplicate or unsorted ids, or a field that is not a well-formed str.
89	    """
90	    if raw == b"":
91	        raise CorruptReceiptError("receipt index is empty")
92	    try:
93	        text = raw.decode("utf-8")
94	    except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:
95	        raise CorruptReceiptError("receipt index is not valid UTF-8") from exc
96	    try:
97	        data = json.loads(text)
98	    except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
99	        raise CorruptReceiptError("receipt index is not valid JSON") from exc
100	
101	    if not isinstance(data, dict):
102	        raise CorruptReceiptError("receipt index must be a JSON object")
103	    if set(data.keys()) != set(_INDEX_KEYS):
104	        raise CorruptReceiptError(
105	            "receipt index must contain exactly the keys 'items' and 'version'"
106	        )
107	    if list(data.keys()) != list(_INDEX_KEYS):
108	        raise CorruptReceiptError(
109	            "receipt index keys must be in the order 'items', 'version'"
110	        )
111	    version = data[VERSION]
112	    # bool is a subclass of int; the version must be a genuine integer.
113	    if isinstance(version, bool) or not isinstance(version, int) or version != 1:
114	        raise CorruptReceiptError("receipt index version must be the integer 1")
115	    raw_items = data[ITEMS]
116	    if not isinstance(raw_items, list):
117	        raise CorruptReceiptError("receipt index items must be an array")
118	
119	    records: list[dict[str, str]] = []
120	    for position, item in enumerate(raw_items):
121	        where = f"receipt index item {position}"
122	        if not isinstance(item, dict):
123	            raise CorruptReceiptError(f"{where} must be a JSON object")
124	        if set(item.keys()) != set(_RECORD_KEYS):
125	            raise CorruptReceiptError(
126	                f"{where} must contain exactly the keys 'audit', 'id' and 'state'"
127	            )
128	        if list(item.keys()) != list(_RECORD_KEYS):
129	            raise CorruptReceiptError(
130	                f"{where} keys must be in the order 'audit', 'id', 'state'"
131	            )
132	        audit_digest = item[AUDIT]
133	        record_id = item[ID]
134	        state_digest = item[STATE]
135	        if not isinstance(record_id, str) or _ID_RE.fullmatch(record_id) is None:
136	            raise CorruptReceiptError(f"{where} has an invalid id")
137	        if not _is_digest(state_digest):
138	            raise CorruptReceiptError(
139	                f"{where} state must be 64 lowercase hex characters"
140	            )
141	        if not _is_digest(audit_digest):
142	            raise CorruptReceiptError(
143	                f"{where} audit must be 64 lowercase hex characters"
144	            )
145	        records.append(
146	            {AUDIT: audit_digest, ID: record_id, STATE: state_digest}
147	        )
148	
149	    ids = [record[ID] for record in records]
150	    if any(left >= right for left, right in zip(ids, ids[1:])):
151	        raise CorruptReceiptError(
152	            "receipt index ids must be unique and sorted ascending"
153	        )
154	
155	    # Reject stray whitespace, non-canonical escapes, and any encoding that
156	    # is not the single compact form of the validated structure.
157	    if _serialize_index(records) != raw:
158	        raise CorruptReceiptError("receipt index is not canonically encoded")
159	    return records
160	
161	
162	def _read_index(path: str) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
163	    try:
164	        with open(path, "rb") as handle:
165	            raw = handle.read()
166	    except FileNotFoundError:
167	        return []
168	    return _parse_index(raw)
169	
170	
171	def _atomic_write(path: str, payload: bytes) -> None:
172	    tmp_path = path + ".tmp"
173	    with open(tmp_path, "wb") as handle:
174	        handle.write(payload)
175	        handle.flush()
176	        os.fsync(handle.fileno())
177	    try:
178	        os.replace(tmp_path, path)
179	    except BaseException:
180	        try:
181	            os.unlink(tmp_path)
182	        except OSError:
183	            pass
184	        raise
185	    fd = os.open(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(path)), os.O_RDONLY)
186	    try:
187	        os.fsync(fd)
188	    finally:
189	        os.close(fd)
190	
191	
192	def put(path: str, receipt: dict[str, str]) -> dict[str, str]:
193	    """Bind ``receipt``'s state and audit digests under its id in the index.
194	
195	    A new id is added and the index is atomically replaced.  Putting the
196	    same id with identical state and audit digests is idempotent: a fresh
197	    dict is returned without touching the file bytes.  The same id with
198	    different digests raises :class:`ValueError` and leaves the file
199	    unchanged.  The returned dict always has the key order
200	    ``audit``, ``id``, ``state``.
201	
202	    Type violations raise :class:`TypeError`; a bad key set, id or digest
203	    format raises :class:`ValueError`; a corrupt index raises
204	    :class:`CorruptReceiptError`; other filesystem errors propagate as
205	    :class:`OSError`.
206	    """
207	    if not isinstance(path, str):
208	        raise TypeError("path must be a str")
209	    record = _validated_receipt(receipt)
210	
211	    records = _read_index(path)
212	    for existing in records:
213	        if existing[ID] == record[ID]:
214	            if (
215	                existing[STATE] != record[STATE]
216	                or existing[AUDIT] != record[AUDIT]
217	            ):
218	                raise ValueError(
219	                    f"receipt id {record[ID]!r} is already bound to a "
220	                    "different state or audit record"
221	                )
222	            # Idempotent replay: brand-new copy, no filesystem change.
223	            return dict(record)
224	
225	    records.append(record)
226	    records.sort(key=lambda entry: entry[ID])
227	    _atomic_write(path, _serialize_index(records))
228	    return dict(record)
229	
230	
231	def get(path: str, id: str) -> dict[str, str] | None:
232	    """Return a fresh copy of the receipt stored under ``id``, or None.
233	
234	    A missing index file or an index without that id yields ``None``.
235	    Type violations raise :class:`TypeError`; a malformed ``id`` raises
236	    :class:`ValueError`; a corrupt index raises
237	    :class:`CorruptReceiptError`; other filesystem errors propagate as
238	    :class:`OSError`.
239	    """
240	    if not isinstance(path, str):
241	        raise TypeError("path must be a str")
242	    if not isinstance(id, str):
243	        raise TypeError("id must be a str")
244	    if _ID_RE.fullmatch(id) is None:
245	        raise ValueError("id must match [A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}")
246	
247	    for record in _read_index(path):
248	        if record[ID] == id:
249	            return dict(record)
250	    return None

1	"""Append-only hash-chained audit log for offline coordination.
2	
3	The audit file is UTF-8 JSONL, one JSON object per line.  Each object has
4	the fixed key set and key order::
5	
6	    detail, hash, kind, prev, seq, source
7	
8	``seq`` starts at 1 and is contiguous; the first record's ``prev`` is 64
9	zero characters and every later ``prev`` equals the previous record's
10	``hash``.  ``hash`` is the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the compact UTF-8 JSON
11	encoding (no whitespace, non-ASCII preserved, no trailing newline) of the
12	record with the ``hash`` key itself removed and the remaining keys in the
13	order above.  Each complete record line is encoded the same way and
14	terminated by ``\\n``.
15	"""
16	
17	from __future__ import annotations
18	
19	import hashlib
20	import json
21	import os
22	from typing import Any
23	
24	DETAIL = "detail"
25	HASH = "hash"
26	KIND = "kind"
27	PREV = "prev"
28	SEQ = "seq"
29	SOURCE = "source"
30	
31	_EVENT_KEYS = (SOURCE, KIND, DETAIL)
32	_RECORD_KEYS = (DETAIL, HASH, KIND, PREV, SEQ, SOURCE)
33	_HASHED_KEYS = (DETAIL, KIND, PREV, SEQ, SOURCE)
34	_KINDS = ("local", "merge", "restore")
35	_ZERO_HASH = "0" * 64
36	
37	
38	class CorruptAuditError(ValueError):
39	    """The audit file exists but its contents are not a valid audit log."""
40	
41	
42	def _compact(obj: Any) -> bytes:
43	    # Same compact UTF-8 JSON rules used for state persistence in storage.py.
44	    return json.dumps(obj, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":")).encode("utf-8")
45	
46	
47	def _validated_event(event: Any) -> dict[str, str]:

"""Append-only hash-chained audit log for offline coordination.

The audit file is UTF-8 JSONL, one JSON object per line.  Each object has
the fixed key set and key order::

    detail, hash, kind, prev, seq, source

``seq`` starts at 1 and is contiguous; the first record's ``prev`` is 64
zero characters and every later ``prev`` equals the previous record's
``hash``.  ``hash`` is the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the compact UTF-8 JSON
encoding (no whitespace, non-ASCII preserved, no trailing newline) of the
record with the ``hash`` key itself removed and the remaining keys in the
order above.  Each complete record line is encoded the same way and
terminated by ``\\n``.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
import os
from typing import Any

DETAIL = "detail"
HASH = "hash"
KIND = "kind"
PREV = "prev"
SEQ = "seq"
SOURCE = "source"

_EVENT_KEYS = (SOURCE, KIND, DETAIL)
_RECORD_KEYS = (DETAIL, HASH, KIND, PREV, SEQ, SOURCE)
_HASHED_KEYS = (DETAIL, KIND, PREV, SEQ, SOURCE)
_KINDS = ("local", "merge", "restore")
_ZERO_HASH = "0" * 64


class CorruptAuditError(ValueError):
    """The audit file exists but its contents are not a valid audit log."""


def _compact(obj: Any) -> bytes:
    # Same compact UTF-8 JSON rules used for state persistence in storage.py.
    return json.dumps(obj, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":")).encode("utf-8")


def _validated_event(event: Any) -> dict[str, str]:
    if not isinstance(event, dict):
        raise TypeError("event must be a dict")
    if set(event.keys()) != set(_EVENT_KEYS):
        raise ValueError(
            "event must contain exactly the keys 'source', 'kind' and 'detail'"
        )
    result: dict[str, str] = {}
    for key in _EVENT_KEYS:
        value = event[key]
        if not isinstance(value, str):
            raise TypeError(f"event {key} must be a str")
        if value == "":
            raise ValueError(f"event {key} must be non-empty")
        result[key] = value
    if result[KIND] not in _KINDS:
        raise ValueError("event kind must be one of 'local', 'merge' or 'restore'")
    return result


def _record_hash(record_without_hash: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
    ordered = {key: record_without_hash[key] for key in _HASHED_KEYS}
    return hashlib.sha256(_compact(ordered)).hexdigest()


def _encode_line(record: dict[str, Any]) -> bytes:
    ordered = {key: record[key] for key in _RECORD_KEYS}
    return _compact(ordered) + b"\n"


def _parse_and_chain(raw: bytes) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Validate every byte of an audit log and return its records.

    Raises :class:`CorruptAuditError` for any UTF-8/JSON decoding failure,
    non-canonical byte encoding, wrong key set, seq/prev/hash chain break,
    or missing line terminator.  Value-domain rules (non-empty fields, the
    kind enum) are enforced on event input by :func:`append`.
    """
    try:
        text = raw.decode("utf-8")
    except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:
        raise CorruptAuditError("audit file is not valid UTF-8") from exc

    records: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    expected_seq = 1
    expected_prev = _ZERO_HASH

    if text == "":
        return records
    # Every record, including the last one, must be newline-terminated; the
    # trailing empty segment is the expected terminator.  Interior empty
    # segments are blank lines and fail canonical re-encoding below.
    lines = text.split("\n")
    if lines[-1] != "":
        raise CorruptAuditError("the last audit line is not terminated by a newline")
    for line_no, line in enumerate(lines[:-1], start=1):
        line_bytes = line.encode("utf-8")
        try:
            data = json.loads(line)
        except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
            raise CorruptAuditError(
                f"audit line {line_no} is not valid JSON"
            ) from exc
        if not isinstance(data, dict):
            raise CorruptAuditError(f"audit line {line_no} is not a JSON object")
        if set(data.keys()) != set(_RECORD_KEYS):
            raise CorruptAuditError(
                f"audit line {line_no} must contain exactly the keys "
                "detail, hash, kind, prev, seq, source"
            )
        detail = data[DETAIL]
        kind = data[KIND]
        prev = data[PREV]
        seq = data[SEQ]
        source = data[SOURCE]
        digest = data[HASH]
        # seq must be a genuine JSON integer (a bool would compare equal to
        # 0/1 and slip past the chain check in Python).
        if isinstance(seq, bool) or not isinstance(seq, int):
            raise CorruptAuditError(f"audit line {line_no} seq must be an int")
        if seq != expected_seq:
            raise CorruptAuditError(
                f"audit line {line_no} seq is {seq}, expected {expected_seq}"
            )
        if prev != expected_prev:
            raise CorruptAuditError(
                f"audit line {line_no} prev does not match the previous hash"
            )
        without_hash = {
            DETAIL: detail,
            KIND: kind,
            PREV: prev,
            SEQ: seq,
            SOURCE: source,
        }
        actual_hash = _record_hash(without_hash)
        if digest != actual_hash:
            raise CorruptAuditError(
                f"audit line {line_no} hash does not match its contents"
            )
        record = {key: None for key in _RECORD_KEYS}
        record[DETAIL] = detail
        record[KIND] = kind
        record[PREV] = prev
        record[SEQ] = seq
        record[SOURCE] = source
        record[HASH] = digest
        # The on-disk bytes must be the single canonical compact encoding:
        # this rejects stray whitespace, non-canonical escapes, and any key
        # order other than the fixed one.
        if _compact({key: record[key] for key in _RECORD_KEYS}) != line_bytes:
            raise CorruptAuditError(
                f"audit line {line_no} is not canonically encoded"
            )
        records.append(record)
        expected_seq += 1
        expected_prev = digest

    return records


def _read_all_records(path: str) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    try:
        with open(path, "rb") as handle:
            raw = handle.read()
    except FileNotFoundError:
        return []
    return _parse_and_chain(raw)


def append(path: str, event: dict[str, str]) -> int:
    """Append one audit event to the log at ``path`` and return its seq.

    Every existing line is verified before anything is written, so a corrupt
    log is never extended.  The new line is flushed and fsynced; when the
    file is newly created its parent directory is fsynced as well.

    Type violations raise :class:`TypeError`; invalid event contents raise
    :class:`ValueError`; a corrupt log raises :class:`CorruptAuditError`;
    other filesystem errors propagate as :class:`OSError`.
    """
    if not isinstance(path, str):
        raise TypeError("path must be a str")
    event_fields = _validated_event(event)

    existed = os.path.exists(path)
    records = _read_all_records(path)
    seq = len(records) + 1
    prev = records[-1][HASH] if records else _ZERO_HASH

    without_hash = {
        DETAIL: event_fields[DETAIL],
        KIND: event_fields[KIND],
        PREV: prev,
        SEQ: seq,
        SOURCE: event_fields[SOURCE],
    }
    digest = _record_hash(without_hash)
    record = dict(without_hash)
    record[HASH] = digest
    line = _encode_line(record)

    with open(path, "ab") as handle:
        handle.write(line)
        handle.flush()
        os.fsync(handle.fileno())

    if not existed:
        fd = os.open(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(path)), os.O_RDONLY)
        try:
            os.fsync(fd)
        finally:
            os.close(fd)

    return seq


def read(path: str) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Return all audit records at ``path`` as a fresh deep-copied list.

    A missing or empty file yields an empty list.  A corrupt log raises
    :class:`CorruptAuditError`; other filesystem errors propagate as
    :class:`OSError`.
    """
    if not isinstance(path, str):
        raise TypeError("path must be a str")
    return _read_all_records(path)

PRUNE_STATUS,
    PRUNE_BEFORE,
    PRUNE_AFTER,
    PRUNE_CHECKPOINT,
    PRUNE_PLAN_DIGEST,
    PRUNE_MOMENT,
    VERSION,
)


def _prune_receipt_invalid(message: str) -> InvalidPruneReceiptError:
    return InvalidPruneReceiptError(f"invalid prune receipt: {message}")


def _verify_prune_receipt(
    receipt: bytes,
    checkpoint: bytes,
    validated_keyring: dict[str, list[dict]],
    moment: int,
) -> dict:
    """Verify one prune receipt against already-validated inputs.

    Shared core of :func:`verify_prune_receipt` and the batch
    :func:`verify_prune_receipts`; the caller owns the argument-type and
    batch-structure validation.  No file is read and no input is
    modified; the result is a fresh dict built solely from authenticated
    receipt material.
    """
    try:
        receipt_payload, receipt_signature = _prune_parse_receipt(receipt)
    except InvalidPruneError as exc:
        raise _prune_receipt_invalid(str(exc)) from exc
    except TypeError as exc:
        raise _prune_receipt_invalid(str(exc)) from exc

    # The complete plan is embedded in the receipt.  Its bytes must be
    # exactly the canonical compact version-1 envelope the receipt bound,
    # parsed independently instead of trusting the embedded shape.
    plan_raw = _prune_compact(receipt_payload[PRUNE_PLAN])
    try:
        plan_payload, plan_signature, _plan_envelope, plan_digest = (
            _prune_parse_plan(plan_raw)
        )
    except InvalidPruneError as exc:
        raise _prune_receipt_invalid(str(exc)) from exc
    except TypeError as exc:
        raise _prune_receipt_invalid(str(exc)) from exc

    checkpoint_digest = hashlib.sha256(checkpoint).hexdigest()
    if plan_payload[PRUNE_CHECKPOINT] != checkpoint_digest:
        raise _prune_receipt_invalid(
            "the embedded plan is not bound to the supplied checkpoint"
        )
    if receipt_payload[PRUNE_CHECKPOINT] != checkpoint_digest:
        raise _prune_receipt_invalid(
            "the receipt is not bound to the supplied checkpoint"
        )

    # The receipt must repeat the plan's delete and retain bindings
    # byte for byte: a missing, extra, reordered or replaced entry is a
    # broken binding.
    if receipt_payload[PRUNE_DELETE] != plan_payload[PRUNE_DELETE]:
        raise _prune_receipt_invalid(
            "receipt delete list does not match its plan"
        )
    if receipt_payload[PRUNE_RETAIN] != plan_payload[PRUNE_RETAIN]:
        raise _prune_receipt_invalid(
            "receipt retain list does not match its plan"
        )

    try:
        cp_payload, cp_signature = _parse_chain_checkpoint(checkpoint)
    except InvalidCheckpointError as exc:
        raise _prune_receipt_invalid(str(exc)) from exc
    except TypeError as exc:
        raise _prune_receipt_invalid(str(exc)) from exc
    issuer = cp_payload[VD_ISSUER]
    key_version = cp_payload[KEY_VERSION]
    entry = _usable_checkpoint_key(
        validated_keyring, issuer, key_version, moment
    )
    secret = entry[SECRET]

    # All three signatures are re-checked with the one current key the
    # checkpoint names: checkpoint, then plan, then receipt, no fallback.
    cp_expected = hmac.new(
        bytes.fromhex(secret),
        _checkpoint_compact(cp_payload),
        hashlib.sha256,
    ).hexdigest()
    if not hmac.compare_digest(cp_expected, cp_signature):
        raise AuthenticationError("chain checkpoint signature does not match")
    plan_expected = hmac.new(
        bytes.fromhex(secret),
        _prune_compact(plan_payload),
        hashlib.sha256,
    ).hexdigest()
    if not hmac.compare_digest(plan_expected, plan_signature):
        raise AuthenticationError("prune plan signature does not match")
    receipt_expected = hmac.new(
        bytes.fromhex(secret),
        _prune_compact(receipt_payload),
        hashlib.sha256,
    ).hexdigest()
    if not hmac.compare_digest(receipt_expected, receipt_signature):
        raise AuthenticationError("prune receipt signature does not match")

    status = receipt_payload[PRUNE_STATUS]
    before_digest = receipt_payload[PRUNE_BEFORE]
    after_digest = receipt_payload[PRUNE_AFTER]
    source_map = plan_payload[PRUNE_SOURCE]
    target_map = plan_payload[PRUNE_TARGET]

    # Locate the unique plan target project from the status and the
    # before/after digests alone; zero or several candidates reject.
    if status == PRUNE_STATUS_PRUNED:
        candidates = [
            project
            for project in plan_payload[PRUNE_DELETE]
            if source_map[project] == before_digest
        ]
        if len(candidates) != 1:
            raise _prune_receipt_invalid(
                "beforeDigest does not uniquely identify one plan source "
                "project"
            )
        project = candidates[0]
        if target_map[project] != after_digest:
            raise _prune_receipt_invalid(
                "afterDigest does not match the plan target for its project"
            )
    else:
        candidates = [
            project
            for project in plan_payload[PRUNE_DELETE]
            if target_map[project] == before_digest
            and target_map[project] == after_digest
        ]
        if len(candidates) != 1:
            raise _prune_receipt_invalid(
                "beforeDigest and afterDigest do not uniquely identify one "
                "plan target project"
            )
        project = candidates[0]

    # Independently regenerate the project's installed version-1 prune
    # marker and hash its complete bytes; the recomputed digest must
    # match both the plan target and the receipt afterDigest, never
    # trusting the receipt's own derived conclusion.
    marker_digest = hashlib.sha256(_prune_pruned_bytes(project)).hexdigest()
    if marker_digest != target_map[project]:
        raise _prune_receipt_invalid(
            "the plan target digest does not match the regenerated prune "
            "marker"
        )
    if marker_digest != after_digest:
        raise _prune_receipt_invalid(
            "the receipt afterDigest does not match the regenerated prune "
            "marker"
        )

    result = {
        PRUNE_PROJECT: project,
        PRUNE_STATUS: status,
        PRUNE_BEFORE: before_digest,
        PRUNE_AFTER: after_digest,
        PRUNE_CHECKPOINT: checkpoint_digest,
        PRUNE_PLAN_DIGEST: plan_digest,
        PRUNE_MOMENT: receipt_payload[PRUNE_MOMENT],
        VERSION: CHAIN_PRUNE_VERSION,
    }
    return {key: result[key] for key in _PRUNE_RECEIPT_RESULT_KEYS}


def verify_prune_receipt(receipt, checkpoint, keyring, moment):
    """Verify one signed chain prune receipt entirely offline.

    Only the ``receipt`` bytes, the sealing ``checkpoint`` bytes, the
    current ``keyring`` and a non-negative verification ``moment`` are
    consulted; no file is read and no argument is modified.  The receipt
    must be a version-1 canonical compact UTF-8 JSON object with
    recursively sorted keys, non-ASCII preserved and no trailing byte,
    carrying exactly ``payload`` and ``signature``; its payload binds
    ``afterDigest``, ``beforeDigest``, ``checkpoint``, ``delete``,
    ``moment``, the complete embedded ``plan``, ``retain``, ``status``
    (``pruned`` or ``duplicate``) and ``version`` (the integer 1).

    The embedded plan must itself be the same canonical version-1
    envelope and must agree with the supplied checkpoint digest, and the
    receipt must repeat the plan's delete projects and retain digests
    exactly -- a missing, extra, reordered or replaced entry is a broken
    binding.  The checkpoint, plan and receipt signatures are all
    recomputed with the single key the checkpoint currently names
    (exact issuer/version, usable at ``moment``), with no fallback.

    The unique plan target project is located solely from the status and
    the before/after digests (zero or several candidates reject); the
    verifier then regenerates that project's version-1 prune marker,
    hashes its complete bytes itself and requires the recomputed digest
    to match both the plan target and the receipt afterDigest -- never
    trusting the receipt's derived conclusion.  A ``pruned`` receipt's
    beforeDigest must match the source archive digest bound in the plan;
    a ``duplicate`` receipt's beforeDigest and afterDigest must both
    match the target marker digest.

    The result is a fresh dict with the fixed key order ``project``,
    ``status``, ``beforeDigest``, ``afterDigest``, ``checkpoint``,
    ``planDigest``, ``moment`` and ``version`` (the integer 1).

    A non-bytes receipt/checkpoint or another wrong public argument type
    raises :class:`TypeError` (a :class:`bool` never poses as an int);
    an illegal moment raises :class:`ValueError`; an illegal encoding,
    key set, version, digest, status or binding raises
    :class:`InvalidPruneReceiptError` (a :class:`ValueError` subclass);
    and unknown, revoked, not-yet-valid or expired credentials or any
    wrong signature raise :class:`AuthenticationError`.
    """
    if not isinstance(receipt, bytes):
        raise TypeError("receipt must be bytes")
    if not isinstance(checkpoint, bytes):
        raise TypeError("checkpoint must be bytes")
    validated_keyring = _validated_keyring(keyring)
    verify_moment = _fe_moment(moment, "moment")
    return _verify_prune_receipt(
        receipt, checkpoint, validated_keyring, verify_moment
    )


def _validated_prune_receipt_items(items: object) -> list[dict]:
    """Validate the receipt-verification batch before any item is checked.

    Each item holds exactly a batch-unique non-empty ``id``, the
    ``receipt`` bytes and the sealing ``checkpoint`` bytes.  Container,
    element or field type faults raise :class:`TypeError`; an empty
    list, an empty or duplicate id or a wrong key set raises
    :class:`ValueError`.
    """
    if not isinstance(items, list):
        raise TypeError("items must be a list")
    if not items:
        raise ValueError("items must be a non-empty list")
    validated: list[dict] = []
    seen: set[str] = set()
    for position, item in enumerate(items):
        where = f"item {position}"
        if not isinstance(item, dict):
            raise TypeError(f"{where} must be a dict")
        if set(item.keys()) != _PRUNE_RECEIPT_ITEM_KEYS:
            raise ValueError(
                f"{where} must contain exactly the keys 'checkpoint', 'id' "
                "and 'receipt'"
            )
        item_id = item[ID]
        if not isinstance(item_id, str):
            raise TypeError(f"{where} id must be a str")
        if item_id == "":
            raise ValueError(f"{where} id must be non-empty")
        if item_id in seen:
            raise ValueError(f"duplicate id {item_id!r}")
        seen.add(item_id)
        receipt = item[PRUNE_RECEIPT]
        if not isinstance(receipt, bytes):
            raise TypeError(f"{where} receipt must be bytes")
        checkpoint = item[PRUNE_CHECKPOINT]
        if not isinstance(checkpoint, bytes):
            raise TypeError(f"{where} checkpoint must be bytes")
        validated.append({
            ID: item_id,
            PRUNE_RECEIPT: receipt,
            PRUNE_CHECKPOINT: checkpoint,
        })
    return validated


def _prune_receipt_report(
    item_id: str, status: str, error: str | None, result: dict | None
) -> dict:
    """One batch receipt-verification report with the fixed key order."""
    return {
        PRUNE_ERROR: error,
        ID: item_id,
        VERDICT_ITEM_RESULT: result,
        STATUS: status,
    }


def _verify_prune_receipt_item(item: dict, validated_keyring: dict,
                               moment: int) -> dict:
    """Verify one prune receipt in isolation and report its outcome."""
    item_id = item[ID]
    try:
        result = _verify_prune_receipt(
            item[PRUNE_RECEIPT],
            item[PRUNE_CHECKPOINT],
            validated_keyring,
            moment,
        )
    except AuthenticationError as exc:
        return _prune_receipt_report(
            item_id, VERIFY_UNAUTHENTICATED, str(exc), None
        )
    except (InvalidPruneReceiptError, InvalidPruneError, TypeError) as exc:
        # A TypeError here can only come from a wrong JSON field type
        # inside the receipt, plan or checkpoint; the public argument
        # types were validated before the batch ran.
        return _prune_receipt_report(
            item_id, _PRUNE_RECEIPT_VERIFY_INVALID, str(exc), None
        )
    return _prune_receipt_report(item_id, _VERIFY_VERIFIED, None, result)


def verify_prune_receipts(items, keyring, moment):
    """Verify a batch of signed chain prune receipts entirely offline.

    ``items`` is a non-empty list; each item is a dict with exactly the
    keys ``id`` (a non-empty str, unique across the batch), ``receipt``
    (the signed receipt bytes :func:`prune_chain_archives` issued) and
    ``checkpoint`` (the sealing checkpoint bytes the receipt's embedded
    plan is bound to).  ``keyring`` follows the
    :func:`apply_signed_remote` rules and ``moment`` is the current
    non-negative integer time.  No file is read or written and no
    argument is modified.

    The whole batch structure, keyring and moment are validated before
    any receipt is verified: container, element or field type faults
    raise :class:`TypeError` (a :class:`bool` never poses as an int) and
    an empty list, an empty or duplicate id, a wrong item key set or an
    illegal moment raises :class:`ValueError`.  Only these batch-level
    faults raise -- one item's failure never stops later items or
    changes an earlier report.

    Each receipt is then verified in input order and in isolation
    through the exact :func:`verify_prune_receipt` rules.  Unknown,
    revoked, not-yet-valid or expired credentials and any wrong
    signature make the item ``unauthenticated``; an illegal encoding,
    key set, version, digest, status or binding makes it ``invalid``; a
    passing receipt is ``verified``.

    The result is a fresh dict with the fixed keys ``items`` and
    ``version`` (the integer 1).  Each report preserves input order and
    carries, in this key order, ``error`` (``None`` when verified,
    otherwise a definite non-empty message), ``id``, ``result`` (a
    fresh single-entry result when verified, otherwise ``None``) and
    ``status``.  Repeated calls return equal but independent results.
    """
    validated_items = _validated_prune_receipt_items(items)
    validated_keyring = _validated_keyring(keyring)
    verify_moment = _fe_moment(moment, "moment")
    return {
        ITEMS: [
            _verify_prune_receipt_item(item, validated_keyring, verify_moment)
            for item in validated_items
        ],
        VERSION: PRUNE_RECEIPTS_VERSION,
    }

1	"""Read-only audit replication batches.
2	
3	A batch is a single UTF-8 compact JSON object (non-ASCII preserved, no
4	whitespace) terminated by exactly one ``\\n``::
5	
6	    {"after":...,"complete":...,"next":...,"records":[...],"version":1}
7	
8	The top-level keys are fixed in the order ``after``, ``complete``,
9	``next``, ``records``, ``version`` and ``version`` is always the integer
10	1.  ``after`` echoes the request's ``after`` argument.  ``records`` holds
11	up to ``limit`` (at most 1000) audit records whose ``seq`` is greater
12	than ``after``, in audit order, each preserving the audit record key
13	order ``detail, hash, kind, prev, seq, source`` and its original values.
14	``next`` is the seq of the last record in the batch, or ``after`` itself
15	when the batch is empty; ``complete`` is true when no record follows the
16	batch, and an empty ``records`` list is only valid when ``complete`` is
17	true.  Batches are generated solely through :func:`audit.read`, so the
18	audit log is never modified and :class:`~offline_coordination.audit.
19	CorruptAuditError` and :class:`OSError` propagate unchanged.
20	
21	:func:`import_batch` validates a batch against this byte contract and
22	appends its records to the local log.  It returns a dict with the fixed
23	key order ``need``, ``next``, ``status``.  When the batch starts beyond
24	the local log (``after`` greater than the local last seq ``L``) nothing is
25	written and ``status`` is ``"missing"`` with ``need`` holding the gap
26	``[L + 1, after]`` and ``next`` set to ``L``.  Otherwise records already
27	present locally must match field by field (a mismatch raises
28	:class:`ValueError`); the matching prefix is skipped idempotently and
29	only the contiguous suffix past ``L`` is appended, linked to the local
30	last hash.  ``need`` is then ``None``, ``next`` is ``max(L, batch.next)``
31	and ``status`` is ``"applied"`` when records were appended, else
32	``"duplicate"``.  Any failure leaves the log untouched.
33	
34	Batches are checked only against the byte contract: canonical encoding, key
35	order, the seq/prev/hash chain and the stored values.  Value-domain rules
36	enforced by :func:`audit.append` on event input (the kind enum, non-empty
37	string fields) are *not* re-enforced here, so every log :func:`audit.read`
38	accepts round-trips through :func:`export_batch`/:func:`import_batch`.  The
39	append itself is atomic: when the write, flush or fsync step raises
40	:class:`OSError` the error propagates unchanged and the log is left
41	byte-identical to its pre-call state (still missing when it was missing).
42	
43	:func:`apply_remote` persists remote state applications in a version-1
44	*ledger*: one UTF-8 compact JSON object (keys sorted lexicographically,
45	exactly one trailing ``\\n``) with the top-level keys ``audit``,
46	``requests``, ``state`` and ``version`` (``version`` is the integer 1).
47	``state`` holds the current :mod:`~offline_coordination.merge` state,
48	``requests`` binds each accepted request id to the digest of its request,
49	and ``audit`` lists one entry per successful application in order; each
50	entry carries ``after``/``before`` state digests, the request ``id`` and
51	``source`` and a contiguous ``seq`` starting at 1, every entry after the
52	first chaining its ``before`` to the previous entry's ``after`` and the

54	request's ``base`` state with empty indexes; any existing file that fails

59	request digest always yields ``duplicate`` from the saved binding alone,

66	its boundary, and an :class:`OSError` at any stage propagates unchanged
67	with the file system restored to its pre-call state.

69	Each commit is additionally backed by a *recovery intent* so a crash of
70	the committing process itself can be reconciled later, across processes.
71	Before anything is replaced, the commit publishes an intent at ``path +
72	".txn"``: one UTF-8 compact JSON object (keys recursively sorted,
73	exactly one trailing ``\n``) recording only ``version`` (the integer 1),

124	:func:`apply_signed_remote` adds an offline-verifiable authentication
125	boundary in front of the same application flow.  It receives the ledger
126	path, a keyring, an envelope and the current moment.  The envelope
127	carries exactly ``node``, ``keyVersion``, ``request`` and ``signature``;
128	the request follows the :func:`apply_remote` contract and its ``source``
129	must equal the envelope's ``node``.  The keyring maps node names to
130	credential entries, each holding exactly ``version`` (a positive integer,
131	unique per node), ``secret`` (64 lowercase hex characters decoding to the
132	32-byte HMAC key), ``notBefore``/``notAfter`` (non-negative integers
133	bounding the validity period, both bounds inclusive) and ``revoked``.
134	The signed payload is the canonical compact UTF-8 JSON encoding of
135	``node``, ``keyVersion`` and ``request`` with every object key
136	recursively sorted lexicographically and non-ASCII preserved; the
137	signature is the lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 computed with the selected key
138	and compared in constant time.  Keys are selected by exact node and
139	version with no fallback: unknown credentials, a revoked, not-yet-valid
140	or expired key, a source/node identity mismatch and a signature mismatch
141	all raise :class:`AuthenticationError` (a :class:`ValueError`) before the
142	ledger is ever read, so a failed verification creates no file.  Replays
143	are authenticated against the *current* keyring, so a later revocation or
144	expiry cannot be bypassed through a historical request binding.  Audit
145	entries committed through :func:`apply_signed_remote` record the verified
146	credentials under ``auth``; entries without ``auth`` remain readable and
147	:func:`apply_remote` keeps its public behaviour and ledger format.
148	
149	:func:`export_proof` and :func:`verify_proof` add offline audit-proof
150	exchange over the same ledger.  A proof is one version-1 UTF-8 compact
151	JSON object -- every object key recursively sorted lexicographically,
152	non-ASCII preserved, exactly one trailing ``\\n`` -- with the top-level
153	keys ``digest``, ``endSeq``, ``entries``, ``firstBefore``, ``lastAfter``,
154	``startSeq`` and ``version``.  ``startSeq``/``endSeq`` name the covered
155	audit range, ``firstBefore`` is the state digest before the first covered
156	entry and ``lastAfter`` the state digest after the last one; ``entries``
157	hold the ledger entries in range unchanged, each carrying ``after``/
158	``before`` state digests, ``id``, ``seq`` and ``source`` with the optional
159	``auth`` binding.  ``digest`` is the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the compact
160	canonical encoding (with no trailing newline) of the proof object with
161	the ``digest`` key itself removed.  :func:`verify_proof` is purely
162	offline: it reads neither the ledger nor the keyring.
163	
164	:func:`compare_proofs` relates two proofs offline, on top of that same
165	purely local verification.  Both arguments are :class:`bytes`; they are
166	first independently checked against the exact :func:`verify_proof`
167	contract, so a non-bytes argument raises :class:`TypeError` and either
168	proof being invalid raises :class:`InvalidProofError` before any
169	comparison.  The ledger, the keyring and the filesystem are never read
170	and neither input is modified.  The result is one version-1 UTF-8
171	compact JSON object -- every object key sorted lexicographically,
172	non-ASCII preserved, exactly one trailing ``\\n`` -- with the fixed
173	top-level keys ``common``, ``conflictSeq``, ``left``, ``overlap``,
174	``relation``, ``right`` and ``version`` (``version`` is the integer 1).
175	``left``/``right`` each carry the proof ``digest`` and its
176	``startSeq``/``endSeq``.  ``overlap`` is the closed shared seq interval
177	``[start, end]`` or ``null`` when the two ranges are disjoint; disjoint
178	ranges never raise and keep both sides' ranges.  With an overlap, the
179	complete entries at every shared seq are compared in ascending seq
180	order -- boundary and proof digests alone are never enough.  If every
181	shared entry matches, ``relation`` is ``"same"`` (identical ranges),
182	``"left-prefix"``/``"right-prefix"`` (same start and the shorter side
183	matches in full, named for the shorter side) or ``"overlap"``
184	otherwise; ``common`` then names the last shared boundary as
185	``{"after", "seq"}`` -- the last common entry's seq and after digest.
186	The first shared seq whose complete entry differs makes ``relation``
187	``"fork"`` with ``conflictSeq`` that earliest seq (never skipped past);
188	``common`` is the last equal entry when an equal entry precedes it, the
189	prior boundary ``{"after", "seq"}`` when the first shared entry already
190	conflicts but its ``before`` digests agree (its seq may be 0), and
191	``null`` when those ``before`` digests differ.  ``conflictSeq`` is
192	``null`` for every non-fork relation.  The bytes are deterministic for
193	equal inputs; swapping the inputs only exchanges ``left``/``right`` and
194	mirrors the prefix direction.
195	
196	:func:`plan_merge` turns that read-only comparison into a read-only merge
197	plan.  It takes both proof byte strings and a conflict ``policy`` --
198	``"left"``, ``"right"`` or ``"manual"``; any other value raises
199	:class:`ValueError` -- and validates every argument type before parsing
200	either proof, so a malformed proof never masks a :class:`TypeError` and an
201	invalid proof still raises :class:`InvalidProofError`.  Disjoint ranges,
202	or a fork whose common boundary cannot be confirmed, raise
203	:class:`ValueError` instead of producing a speculative plan.  Only
204	complete entries strictly after the common boundary become steps: an
205	unforked history accepts the longer side's tail as an ``extension``; a
206	fork accepts the selected side's tail (``selected``) and rejects the
207	other (``rejected``), while ``manual`` marks both tails ``manual`` and
208	references them from ``unresolved``.  The plan is one version-1 UTF-8
209	compact JSON object -- keys recursively sorted, non-ASCII preserved,
210	exactly one trailing ``\\n`` -- with the top-level keys ``common``,
211	``left``, ``policy``, ``relation``, ``right``, ``steps``, ``unresolved``
212	and ``version``; steps carry the original entries unchanged and are
213	ordered by ascending seq with the left side first on ties.  The plan is
214	byte-stable for equal inputs, mirrors left/right when the proofs are
215	swapped together with a ``left``/``right`` policy, and never touches the
216	filesystem or the inputs.
217	
218	:func:`resolve_merge` closes a ``manual`` plan read-only.  It takes the
219	plan byte string, the same two proofs and a list of decisions; only a
220	``manual`` plan produced by :func:`plan_merge` for exactly those proofs
221	may be resolved -- a plan from any other policy is a structurally valid
222	version-1 plan whose steps differ from the regenerated manual plan and
223	is therefore rejected as stale before any decision is considered.
224	A structurally invalid plan (encoding, duplicate keys, version-1
225	structure) raises :class:`InvalidPlanError`; a structurally valid plan
226	that is not byte-for-byte the manual plan regenerated from the proofs
227	(digest, relation, common boundary, side summaries, steps or unresolved
228	references) raises :class:`StalePlanError`; both are
229	:class:`ValueError` subclasses.  Each decision carries only ``side``,
230	``seq`` and ``action`` (``"accept"`` or ``"reject"``), resolving one
231	unresolved reference; missing, duplicate, extra or out-of-range
232	references and illegal choices raise :class:`InvalidResolutionError`
233	(a :class:`ValueError`).  Accepted entries must chain contiguously from
234	the common boundary -- at most one accepted side per seq, no acceptance
235	past a rejected seq, an unbroken seq and digest chain.  The result is
236	one version-1 compact JSON object with the top-level keys ``common``,
237	``left``, ``planDigest``, ``relation``, ``right``, ``steps``,
238	``unresolved`` and ``version``; manual steps become
239	``accept``/``reject`` with the fixed reasons ``manual-accepted``/
240	``manual-rejected``, non-manual steps, carried audit entries and ``auth``
241	bindings are unchanged, ``unresolved`` is empty and ``planDigest`` is the
242	lowercase hex SHA-256 of the complete source plan bytes.  Resolution is
243	deterministic, mirrors under a left/right swap with matching decisions,
244	and never touches the filesystem or the inputs.
245	
246	:func:`commit_resolution` is the write entry point that lands a manual
247	resolution in the ledger.  It takes the ledger path, the canonical
248	resolution bytes, the original plan bytes, both proofs and the landing
249	material -- the final ``state`` plus ``requests`` binding every accepted
250	entry id to its request digest.  Both proofs are verified offline and
251	the plan and resolution are checked against the freshly regenerated
252	manual plan (:class:`StalePlanError` otherwise, without touching the
253	ledger); the ledger itself must still sit at the resolution's common
254	boundary (:class:`StaleLedgerError`, a :class:`ValueError`).  A fully
255	identical replay is recognized before that staleness check and returns
256	``duplicate``; a resolution accepting nothing returns ``unchanged`` and
257	writes nothing.  Otherwise the final state, the request bindings and
258	the contiguous accepted entries -- rejected entries never enter the
259	audit -- are written in one fail-safe replacement, returning
260	``applied``.  The result carries only ``next``, ``resolutionDigest``
261	and ``status``.

263	:func:`recover_authorized` puts an offline-verifiable authorization
264	boundary and a durable operation audit around the same batch recovery.
265	It takes the ledger path list, a keyring, a ticket, the current moment
266	and the recovery audit path.  The ticket is one UTF-8 compact JSON
267	object -- every object key recursively sorted lexicographically,
268	non-ASCII preserved, no trailing newline or any other trailing byte --
269	carrying exactly ``payload`` and ``signature``.  The payload holds exactly ``issuer``,
270	``keyVersion``, ``nonce``, ``notBefore``, ``notAfter`` and the ordered
271	``paths``; the signature is the lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 of the
272	canonical compact payload encoding, computed with the key the keyring
273	binds to the exact issuer and version (the
274	:func:`apply_signed_remote` keyring rules) and compared in constant
275	time.  The command paths must equal the ticket paths item for item --
276	never expanded, reordered or implicitly normalized.  Unknown
277	credentials, a revoked, not-yet-valid or expired key or ticket, a path
278	mismatch and a signature mismatch all raise :class:`AuthenticationError`
279	before any ledger is read, so a failed authorization creates no audit
280	record, consumes no nonce and leaves no temporary file.  Type faults in
281	the arguments raise :class:`TypeError` (a :class:`bool` never poses as
282	``moment``); a malformed ticket key set, nonce, validity interval,
283	encoding or signature format raises :class:`ValueError`.
284	
285	Once authorized, the batch runs in the :func:`recover_many` order with
286	the same per-ledger isolation and the same public item structure, and
287	every step is recorded in an append-only recovery audit at the given
288	path: a canonical JSONL hash chain (recursively sorted keys, one
289	trailing ``\\n`` per record, each record chaining the previous record's
290	SHA-256) where every record is written, flushed and synced before the
291	step it gates.  The first use of a nonce persists a ``batch`` header
292	binding the ticket digest, the issuer and the ordered paths; each
293	ledger then gets a ``before`` record (original digest, recovery phase,
294	planned action) and an ``after`` record (new digest, status, failure
295	category).  An :class:`OSError` while reading the audit or writing,
296	flushing or syncing a record propagates unchanged and leaves a
297	consistent, retryable chain prefix.  Re-entering with the same nonce
298	and the same ticket reuses the recorded results and only continues the
299	paths not yet settled; a process interrupted after a recovery but
300	before its result record is completed from the recorded action and
301	digests, without repeating side effects.  The same nonce bound to a
302	different ticket raises :class:`ReplayError` (a :class:`ValueError`)
303	without modifying any file, and a corrupt chain raises
304	:class:`CorruptRecoveryAuditError` (a :class:`ValueError`).
305	
306	:func:`export_recovery_audit` pages the recovery audit read-only:
307	``after``/``limit`` select the window, the whole chain is validated
308	and a missing audit is treated as an empty chain.
309	
310	:func:`export_recovery_checkpoint` adds an offline signature anchor
311	over the same chain.  It takes the audit path, a keyring, an issuer,
312	a key version and a moment, reads and validates the whole chain
313	read-only and returns one canonical compact UTF-8 JSON object -- keys
314	recursively sorted, non-ASCII preserved, no trailing newline or any
315	other trailing byte -- carrying exactly ``payload`` and ``signature``.
316	The payload binds exactly ``issuer``, ``keyVersion``, ``lastSeq``,
317	``moment``, ``tail`` and ``version`` (the integer 1); ``lastSeq`` is
318	the chain's last seq (0 for a missing audit) and ``tail`` the last
319	record hash (the zero hash for an empty chain).  The signature is the
320	lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 of the canonical compact payload bytes under
321	the key the keyring binds to the exact issuer and version, with no
322	fallback; unknown credentials and a revoked, not-yet-valid or expired
323	key raise :class:`AuthenticationError`, a corrupt chain raises
324	:class:`CorruptRecoveryAuditError` and an :class:`OSError` while
325	reading propagates unchanged.
326	
327	:func:`verify_recovery_page` verifies a paging dict against such a
328	checkpoint entirely offline: it reads no file.  The checkpoint is
329	parsed and its HMAC is verified against the current keyring (exact
330	issuer/version, usable at the given moment, so a later revocation or
331	expiry rejects the checkpoint as it does a replay); the moment bound
332	into the payload is part of the signed anchor itself and needs no
333	equality with the verification time.  The first round passes no cursor
334	and the page's ``after`` must be zero; every later round passes the
335	``{"digest", "next", "tail"}`` cursor built from the previous result,
336	requiring ``after`` to equal the cursor's ``next``, the first record
337	to chain to the cursor's ``tail`` and the cursor ``digest`` to equal
338	this checkpoint's SHA-256 digest, so a cursor can never resume
339	another checkpoint.  Every page's records must be contiguous from
340	``after + 1`` (no gap, reordering or duplicate), hash-correct and
341	chained inside the page and across its boundaries, and verification
342	never crosses the signed ``lastSeq``; before that seq an empty page
343	or a wrong ``complete`` flag is rejected as an invalid page.  The
344	result carries the fixed keys ``digest``, ``lastSeq``, ``status`` and
345	``tail``: reaching the signed tail yields ``"verified"``, every
346	earlier page ``"continue"``.  An empty checkpoint accepts only an
347	empty page starting at zero and reports seq 0, the zero hash and
348	``"verified"``.  Type faults raise :class:`TypeError` (a bool never
349	poses as an int), keyring faults raise :class:`ValueError`,
350	checkpoint faults raise :class:`InvalidRecoveryCheckpointError` and
351	page or cursor faults raise :class:`InvalidRecoveryPageError`; both
352	format errors subclass :class:`ValueError`.  No input or file is
353	modified.
354	
355	:func:`verify_recovery_checkpoints` verifies a whole batch of
356	checkpoints offline, in input order, and never reads a file.  Each
357	item carries exactly a non-empty, batch-unique ``id``, the
358	``checkpoint`` bytes and the ordered, non-empty ``pages`` exported
359	for that checkpoint; the batch is validated in full before any item
360	is verified, so a container, field or element type fault raises
361	:class:`TypeError` and an empty list, an empty or duplicate id or an
362	empty page list raises :class:`ValueError` without producing any
363	result.  Every item is then verified in isolation from a zero cursor
364	through the exact :func:`verify_recovery_page` paging rules, each
365	round resuming from a cursor bound to the same checkpoint digest and
366	the previous page's chain tail, and one item's failure never stops
367	the later items.  Each checkpoint selects its key by its own exact
368	issuer and version with no fallback, so checkpoints signed before
369	and after a key rotation verify independently in the same batch as
370	long as the keyring retains both versions.  An item that reaches the
371	signed ``lastSeq`` must have no further pages; an item whose pages
372	run out earlier is ``incomplete`` and keeps its verified boundary.
373	Every item reports ``id``, the checkpoint ``digest``, the signed
374	``issuer`` and ``keyVersion`` (both ``None`` when the checkpoint
375	does not parse), the verified ``boundary`` (``None`` when nothing
376	was verified), a ``status`` of ``verified``, ``incomplete``,
377	``invalid-checkpoint``, ``invalid-page`` or ``unauthenticated`` and
378	an ``error`` (``None`` exactly when the item verified).  The result
379	is a fresh dict with the fixed key order ``items``, ``version``
380	(the integer 1); only batch-level or keyring-level faults raise,
381	never one item's verification failure.

383	:func:`adjudicate_recovery` turns those per-site verification results
384	into one offline aggregate verdict, still reading no file.  It takes a
385	non-empty ``items`` list, a ``policy``, a ``keyring`` and ``moment``.
386	Each item contains exactly a non-empty, batch-unique ``id`` and
387	``attestation`` bytes -- one canonical compact UTF-8 JSON object with
388	recursively sorted keys, non-ASCII preserved and no trailing newline
389	or any other trailing byte, carrying exactly ``payload`` and
390	``signature``.  The payload binds exactly ``batch``, ``site``,
391	``keyVersion`` and ``result`` with no extra fields; ``result`` follows
392	the public single-item :func:`verify_recovery_checkpoints` report
393	shape (``boundary``, ``digest``, ``error``, ``id``, ``issuer``,
394	``keyVersion``, ``status``).  Every legal single-item result is
395	accepted: a ``verified`` result always carries the checkpoint
396	identity, positive key version and signed boundary, while a
397	non-verified result may carry null ``issuer``/``keyVersion`` (when the
398	checkpoint did not parse) or a null boundary -- its identity, digest,
399	boundary and status are preserved on the report -- and only a
400	``verified`` result may count.
401	The policy binds the authorized ``batch``, a positive ``threshold`` no
402	greater than the number of its sites and, per non-empty site, the
403	non-empty set of positive key versions that site may use; the keyring
404	and moment keep their existing structure, validity and revocation
405	rules.  The signature is the lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 of the
406	canonical compact payload bytes under the key selected by the exact
407	site and version with no fallback.  A wrong batch or unauthorized
408	site/version, unavailable, revoked, not-yet-valid or expired
409	credentials, a bad signature and a non-verified result each reject the
410	packet with a fixed reason and never count; a single packet with
411	illegal encoding, key sets or fields is rejected on its own as
412	``invalid-attestation`` and never blocks the other packets.  For one
413	site an identical valid packet -- the complete embedded result
414	(``boundary``, ``digest``, ``error``, ``id``, ``issuer``,
415	``keyVersion`` and ``status``) equal on every field -- counts once
416	and further copies are ``duplicate``, while any differing valid
417	result (even one sharing digest and boundary) is a
418	self-``contradiction``; valid packets from different sites must
419	agree on both digest and boundary, since any disagreement is a fork a
420	majority cannot mask.  The result is one canonical compact UTF-8 JSON
421	object (sorted keys, non-ASCII preserved, no trailing byte) with the
422	top-level keys ``boundary``, ``digest``, ``items``, ``status``,
423	``threshold`` and ``version`` (the integer 1): any contradiction or
424	cross-site fork yields ``conflicted`` with a null digest and boundary,
425	a unique agreed result from at least the threshold of distinct sites
426	yields ``accepted``, and every other case ``insufficient``.  Every
427	packet is reported -- sorted stably by site then id -- with its
428	identity, conclusion, fixed reason and verified boundary, and the
429	verdict is independent of input order.

538	:func:`verify_fork_decisions` verifies a non-empty batch of those

553	commands are unchanged.

555	:func:`plan_fork_execution` turns one sealed, accepted disposition into
556	a site execution plan entirely offline.  It re-verifies the decision
557	through the exact :func:`verify_fork_decision` rules against the current
558	keyring at the generation moment and only an ``accepted`` decision can
559	be planned (any other verdict raises :class:`ValueError`).  The plan is
560	one canonical compact UTF-8 JSON object (recursively sorted keys,
561	non-ASCII preserved, no trailing byte) binding exactly ``action``,
562	``boundaries``, ``decisionDigest``, ``expiresAt``, ``generatedAt``,
563	``operations``, ``policyDigest`` and ``version``; it carries every fork
564	boundary and the deduplicated, ascending target domains as exactly one
565	idempotent operation per target and no un-adopted proof material.  Each
566	operation's ``operationId`` is the SHA-256 over the decision digest,
567	action, target and the canonical bytes of its related boundaries; an
568	``isolate`` precondition requires ``{"state": "active"}`` while a
569	``rollback`` binds ``{"base", "upstream"}`` (the base receipt digest and
570	the forking upstream).
571	
572	:func:`confirm_fork_execution` aggregates the per-site execution
573	receipts into one signed confirmation, reading and writing no file.  It
574	checks the plan packet, its decision and policy digests, the
575	still-accepted decision and the regenerated plan.  Each receipt binds
576	the plan digest, operation id, executing site and key version, site
577	version, execution moment, previous-state digest and one result
578	(``executed``/``rejected``/``failed``), an executed receipt also binding
579	the post-state digest.  The receipt site must equal the operation
580	target and its exact site/version key must be usable at both the
581	execution and aggregation moments.  A replaced verdict, unknown
582	operation, out-of-window execution, previous mismatch or same-site
583	out-of-order receipt rejects only that item with a fixed reason, as do
584	invalid or time-invalid credentials or a wrong signature; a
585	structurally illegal receipt only records ``invalid-receipt``.  The same
586	receipt digest counts once (``duplicate``); different valid results or
587	post-state digests for one operation are a ``contradiction``.
588	Contradictions, explicit rejections, missing/failed operations and full
589	success yield ``conflicted``, ``rejected``, ``partial`` and
590	``confirmed``.  The canonical ``{payload, signature}`` packet binds the
591	aggregator identity, the complete plan, the original-order receipt
592	digests, per-item reasons, per-operation conclusions and the overall
593	status; the signature is the HMAC-SHA256 of the canonical payload under
594	the exact aggregator key.
595	
596	:func:`verify_fork_confirmation` and the batch
597	:func:`verify_fork_confirmations` re-check those packets entirely
598	offline.  Verification validates the encoding and key sets, regenerates
599	and compares the plan, re-derives the duplicate/contradiction markings,
600	per-operation conclusions and overall status purely from the bound
601	receipts and reasons, and checks the aggregator HMAC against the exact
602	issuer/version key usable at the verification moment, so later
603	revocation or expiry rejects it.  Batch items are validated up front
604	and handled in strict input order and isolation as ``verified``,
605	``invalid`` or ``unauthenticated``.  Across this layer a parameter,
606	container or public field type fault raises :class:`TypeError` (a
607	:class:`bool` never poses as an int); an empty value, duplicate
608	identifier or illegal moment raises :class:`ValueError`; an illegal
609	plan/packet encoding, digest, order or binding raises
610	:class:`InvalidForkExecutionError` (a :class:`ValueError` subclass, with
611	a structurally bad receipt only recorded as ``invalid-receipt``); and
612	unknown, revoked, not-yet-valid or expired credentials or a wrong
613	signature raise :class:`AuthenticationError`.  No file is read or
614	written and every existing public interface is unchanged.
615	
616	:func:`seal_chain_checkpoint` seals a pruned *chain checkpoint* over
617	one verified, accepted and unforked target chain of a
618	:func:`verify_decision_chains` batch, so a verifier can keep checking
619	the chain after the prefix certificates and rounds are dropped.  The
620	checkpoint is one canonical compact UTF-8 JSON object carrying exactly
621	``payload`` and ``signature``; the payload binds the root digest, the
622	stable head digest, the height, the head status, the settlement
623	(``commonDigest``) and plan digests, the head policy digest and
624	version, the head effective moment, the ordered packet digests, the
625	per-stage policy digest history, the ordered evidence prefix digests
626	and the sealing moment, and the signature is the HMAC-SHA256 of the
627	canonical payload under the exact issuer/version key.  A target that
628	is not verified, accepted and fork-free raises :class:`ValueError`.
629	
630	:func:`verify_chain_suffix` continues verification offline from just
631	the checkpoint, the successor packets past the checkpoint head, the
632	per-stage policies and the shared material.  An empty suffix returns
633	the sealed stable head; otherwise the first successor's predecessor
634	digest must equal the checkpoint head digest, its evidence prefix
635	count and digests must match the checkpoint and every hop follows the
636	exact :func:`verify_decision_chain` rules.  The stage policies start
637	at the checkpoint head policy and a version regression is always
638	rejected.  The result maps ``rootDigest``, ``headDigest``, ``height``,
639	``policyVersion``, ``status`` and ``checkpointDigest``.
640	
641	:func:`verify_chain_suffixes` verifies a batch of such items (each
642	exactly ``id``, ``checkpoint``, ``successors`` and ``policies``) in
643	input order and isolation, reporting ``verified``,
644	``invalid-checkpoint``, ``invalid-suffix``, ``unauthenticated`` or
645	``conflicted``; the same predecessor digest pointing at two distinct
646	successors across the verified trajectories is a fork (a mere prefix
647	extension is not) and reclassifies every verified chain crossing it as
648	``conflicted`` with its result kept.  Checkpoint binding faults raise
649	:class:`InvalidCheckpointError`, suffix faults
650	:class:`InvalidChainError` and credential or signature faults
651	:class:`AuthenticationError`.  None of the three entry points reads or
652	writes a file or modifies an input, and the existing chain, anchor,
653	command and status behaviour is unchanged.
654	"""
655	
656	from __future__ import annotations
657	
658	import copy
659	import hashlib
660	import hmac
661	import json
662	import os
663	import re
664	from typing import BinaryIO, Callable
665	
666	from offline_coordination import audit, merge, storage
667	
668	AFTER = "after"
669	COMPLETE = "complete"
670	NEED = "need"
671	NEXT = "next"
672	RECORDS = "records"
673	STATUS = "status"
674	VERSION = "version"
